subject: Dedicated SKU mapping: workload tilt (memory-heavy vs throughput) — proposal
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Elyse Park <elyse@deepcove.ai>, Procurement <procurement@deepcove.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated SKU mapping: workload tilt (memory-heavy vs throughput) — initial ask

Hi Elyse / procurement team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion I promised a quick mapping exercise so you can see how we would size Dedicated capacity across H100 / A100 / L4 given DeepCove's mixed workload profile. Attached is a short CSV with representative query profiles (p95 tokens, context window, batchability, memory working set).

Quick context on what matters for SKU selection:
- H100: best raw throughput for large-context transformer workloads, highest memory per GPU with good fp16/4-bit perf for generative and retrieval-augmented flows.
- A100: solid balance of memory and throughput for mid-sized models and stable driver stack; lower unit cost than H100 in many clouds.
- L4: cost-efficient for small-to-medium models, excellent latency per-dollar for short-context conversational workloads but limited memory for large context KV.

Can you confirm:
1) Which percent of queries are generation vs embeddings vs rerank (ballpark)?
2) Peak concurrency target (p95) you want us to design for?
3) Any strict retention/eviction policies that force larger KV cache sizes per query?

I attached the CSV (deepcove_query_profile.csv) — if you can fill or confirm the highlighted rows I’ll loop in Lev/Infra for an initial SKU allocation.

Next step goal: present a concise SKU recommendation and a mutual action plan for Dedicated procurement by EOW next week.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Elyse Park <elyse@deepcove.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-02T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated SKU mapping: workload tilt (memory-heavy vs throughput) — initial ask

Connor, thanks — sending quick clarifications:
- Workload split (approx): generation 55%, embeddings 30%, rerank 15%. Generation mix is 70% short conversations (<=512 tokens) and 30% long form completions (1k-8k tokens) used for summarization pipelines.
- Peak concurrency target: ~450 concurrent requests across the fleet, p95 latency target 350ms for short convs, 1.2s for long-form.
- KV/cache: we do keep session contexts hot for top 10% of users — that implies larger per-GPU KV footprint for long-form.
- Compliance note: prefer no cross-tenant shared KV persistence; isolated slices preferred.

Procurement (cc) will follow up with PO cadence if the SKU/cost looks reasonable.

— Elyse
Head of ML Ops, DeepCove Labs
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-03T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated SKU mapping — DeepCove profile (need recommendation)

Lauren / Ben — forwarding DeepCove's profile. TL;DR: mixed workload, generation-heavy, 450 concurrency target, persistent KV for 10% of sessions. They want isolated slices. Can you sketch SKU allocation and an ops note about fallbacks?

Attachments: deepcove_query_profile.csv

Key constraints I care about:
- Keep p95 latency targets under 350ms for short convs.
- Avoid over-provisioning large memory GPUs unless necessary (cost sensitivity).
- Can we propose a Hybrid allocation: majority A100 for cost/perf balance, small H100 pool for long-form and heavy KV, L4 for low-cost conversational burst capacity?

Thanks — need a short deck + numbers I can share with procurement by Fri.

Connor
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-03T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated SKU mapping — DeepCove profile (recommendation)

Connor, Ben — ran the profile through the sizing heuristics. High-level recommendation: Hybrid SKU mix with clear routing/fallback rules. Summary below (numbers are illustrative capacity units mapped to expected concurrency):

1) Primary pool — A100 (approx 65% of committed vGPUs)
- Role: steady-state generation and embeddings, handles most medium-context sessions.
- Why: good memory (40GB) and throughput for most of their mixes; cheaper than H100 for bulk.
- Benefit: simpler driver stack and predictable performance across clouds.

2) Memory-first pool — H100 (approx 20% of committed vGPUs)
- Role: long-form summarization jobs, large KV hot sessions, multi-model ensembles where memory density matters.
- Why: large memory headroom and better scaling for mixed-precision kernels on long contexts.
- Ops note: pin these to reserved slices for isolation as requested.

3) Cost-burst pool — L4 (approx 15% of committed vGPUs)
- Role: very short-context conversational traffic and latency-sensitive p95 for small queries.
- Why: best latency per-dollar for <=512 token workloads; use autoscaling burst policies.

Routing policy (high level):
- Short convs (<512 tokens): route to L4 if capacity, else A100.
- Medium convs (512-2k): A100.
- Long-form (>2k) or KV-heavy: H100.

Quantization / model splitting: prefer int4/knobs on A100 and L4 where quality tests pass; keep H100 running fp16/amp for longest contexts.

Estimated footprint (starting commit): 30 A100-equivalent units, 9 H100-equivalent units, 6 L4-equivalent units (adjust as we observe actual QPS).

I will attach a quick spreadsheet (sku-mapping-draft-v1.xlsx) with concurrency math and cost delta vs pure-A100 baseline.

Lauren
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated SKU mapping: workload tilt (memory-heavy vs throughput) — proposal

Elyse / Procurement team — thanks for the details. Based on Lauren/Ben's sizing here's our recommended starting Dedicated allocation and a lightweight mutual action plan: 

Recommended starting allocation (commit):
- A100 pool: commit 30 units (handles ~65% of steady-state generation and embeddings)
- H100 pool: commit 9 units (isolated slices for long-form and KV-heavy sessions)
- L4 pool: commit 6 units (autoscaling burst for latency-sensitive short convs)

Routing & QoS rules (summary):
- Route short convs (<512 tokens) to L4 first, overflow to A100.
- Route medium (512-2k) to A100.
- Long-form (>2k) and KV-hot sessions pinned to H100 slices.
- KV isolation: H100 slices are tenant-isolated to respect your no-shared-persistence requirement.

Operational notes:
- We will enable prefix/KV caching on A100 to reduce token costs for repeated prompts; H100 gets larger KV allocations but less aggressive eviction.
- Graceful fallback: when H100 depleted, fall back to A100 with a slight QoS warning; degrade long-form generation to chunked outputs to preserve latency SLOs.

Next steps and timeline:
1) Procurement review & PO signal — please advise expected approval date (Procurement).
2) Provisioning window — 7 business days after PO for reserved slices and basic routing config.
3) Pilot observability — 2 weeks of telemetry to tune ratios, then adjust commit at 30-day mark.

Attached: sku-mapping-draft-v1.xlsx, deepcove_query_profile.csv.
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/RDW-2691

If this looks good I’ll draft a concise contract addendum reflecting the committed SKUs and reserved slice isolation.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
